On market day, peasants and their wives were walking along every road toward the little town of Goderville. <break time="0.8s" /> Bent by years of hard work in the fields, the men moved slowly with long, heavy steps. <break time="0.8s" /> The women carried baskets full of chickens and ducks, hurrying to the square where the market was held. <break time="0.8s" /> Among them was Maître Hauchecorne of Bréauté, who had just arrived at the edge of the town. <break time="0.8s" /> Walking toward the square, he noticed a little piece of string lying on the ground. <break time="0.8s" /> Like every true Norman, he believed that anything useful should be picked up, so he bent down slowly. <break time="0.8s" /> His old back hurt from rheumatism, but he took the string from the ground and began to roll it up carefully. <break time="0.8s" /> Just then he saw Maître Malandain, the harness maker, watching him from the doorway of his shop. <break time="0.8s" /> The two men had once quarreled about a halter, and they had never forgiven each other since that day. <break time="0.8s" /> Feeling ashamed to be seen picking up string, Hauchecorne quickly hid it in his pocket and pretended to search the ground.

장날에 농부들과 그 아내들이. <break time="0.8s" /> 길마다 걸어가고 있었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 작은 읍내 고데르빌을 향해. <break time="0.8s" /> 들판에서 여러 해 힘들게 일해 몸이 굽은 채. <break time="0.8s" /> 남자들은 느릿느릿 걸었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 길고 무거운 걸음으로. <break time="0.8s" /> 여자들은 바구니를 들고 갔다. <break time="0.8s" /> 닭과 오리가 가득 든. <break time="0.8s" /> 광장으로 서둘러 가면서. <break time="0.8s" /> 장이 열리는. <break time="0.8s" /> 그들 가운데에는 브레오테 마을의 오슈코른 영감이 있었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그는 막 도착한 참이었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 읍내 어귀에. <break time="0.8s" /> 광장 쪽으로 걸어가다가. <break time="0.8s" /> 그는 작은 끈 한 조각을 보았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 땅바닥에 놓여 있는. <break time="0.8s" /> 진짜 노르망디 사람들이 다 그렇듯. <break time="0.8s" /> 그는 믿었다 쓸모 있는 것은 무엇이든 주워야 한다고. <break time="0.8s" /> 그래서 그는 천천히 허리를 굽혔다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그의 늙은 허리가 아팠다. <break time="0.8s" /> 류머티즘 때문에. <break time="0.8s" /> 하지만 그는 땅에서 끈을 집어 들었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 그것을 조심스럽게 감기 시작했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 바로 그때. <break time="0.8s" /> 그는 말랑댕 영감을 보았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그는 마구 장인이었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 말랑댕이 자기를 지켜보는 모습을. <break time="0.8s" /> 자기 가게 문간에서. <break time="0.8s" /> 두 사람은 예전에 다툰 적이 있었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 고삐 하나를 두고. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 서로를 한 번도 용서하지 않았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그날 이후로. <break time="0.8s" /> 그는 부끄러웠다. <break time="0.8s" /> 끈을 줍다가 남에게 들킨 것이. <break time="0.8s" /> 오슈코른은 재빨리 그것을 감추었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 주머니 속에. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 땅을 뒤지는 척했다.

The square was crowded. <break time="0.8s" /> With people and animals. <break time="0.8s" /> And the air was full of shouting, laughing. <break time="0.8s" /> And the smell of cattle. <break time="0.8s" /> Farmers bargained for a long time. <break time="0.8s" /> Over every cow and pig. <break time="0.8s" /> Always afraid that someone might cheat them. <break time="0.8s" /> At noon the crowd went to Jourdains inn. <break time="0.8s" /> Where a great fire was roasting. <break time="0.8s" /> Chickens, pigeons, and legs of lamb. <break time="0.8s" /> The diners ate and drank happily. <break time="0.8s" /> Talking loudly. <break time="0.8s" /> About the weather and the harvest. <break time="0.8s" /> Suddenly a drum sounded. <break time="0.8s" /> In the courtyard. <break time="0.8s" /> And everyone except a few who did not care. <break time="0.8s" /> Ran to the doors and windows. <break time="0.8s" /> The town crier announced that a black leather pocketbook had been lost. <break time="0.8s" /> That morning. <break time="0.8s" /> On the road to Beuzeville. <break time="0.8s" /> It held five hundred francs. <break time="0.8s" /> And some business papers. <break time="0.8s" /> And the finder would receive. <break time="0.8s" /> A reward of twenty francs. <break time="0.8s" /> The owner Maître Houlbrèque of Manneville. <break time="0.8s" /> Asked the finder. <break time="0.8s" /> To bring it to the mayors office or to him. <break time="0.8s" /> As the diners were guessing. <break time="0.8s" /> Who might find it. <break time="0.8s" /> A police officer appeared. <break time="0.8s" /> At the door of the dining room. <break time="0.8s" /> He asked for Maître Hauchecorne of Bréauté. <break time="0.8s" /> And told him that the mayor wished to speak with him. <break time="0.8s" /> At once.

The square was crowded with people and animals, and the air was full of shouting, laughing, and the smell of cattle. <break time="0.8s" /> Farmers bargained for a long time over every cow and pig, always afraid that someone might cheat them. <break time="0.8s" /> At noon, the crowd went to Jourdains inn, where a great fire was roasting chickens, pigeons, and legs of lamb. <break time="0.8s" /> The diners ate and drank happily, talking loudly about the weather and the harvest. <break time="0.8s" /> Suddenly a drum sounded in the courtyard, and everyone except a few who did not care ran to the doors and windows. <break time="0.8s" /> The town crier announced that a black leather pocketbook had been lost that morning on the road to Beuzeville. <break time="0.8s" /> It held five hundred francs and some business papers, and the finder would receive a reward of twenty francs. <break time="0.8s" /> The owner, Maître Houlbrèque of Manneville, asked the finder to bring it to the mayors office or to him. <break time="0.8s" /> As the diners were guessing who might find it, a police officer appeared at the door of the dining room. <break time="0.8s" /> He asked for Maître Hauchecorne of Bréauté and told him that the mayor wished to speak with him at once.

광장은 붐볐다. <break time="0.8s" /> 사람과 짐승들로. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 공기는 가득했다 고함 소리와 웃음소리. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 소 냄새로. <break time="0.8s" /> 농부들은 오랫동안 흥정했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 소 한 마리, 돼지 한 마리를 두고. <break time="0.8s" /> 늘 두려워하면서 누군가 자기를 속일까 봐. <break time="0.8s" /> 정오에 사람들은 주르댕의 여관으로 갔다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그곳에서는 커다란 불이 굽고 있었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 닭과 비둘기와 양 다리를. <break time="0.8s" /> 식사하는 사람들은 즐겁게 먹고 마셨다. <break time="0.8s" /> 큰 소리로 이야기하면서. <break time="0.8s" /> 날씨와 수확에 대해. <break time="0.8s" /> 갑자기 북소리가 울렸다. <break time="0.8s" /> 안마당에서. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 관심 없는 몇 사람을 빼고 모두가. <break time="0.8s" /> 문과 창가로 달려갔다. <break time="0.8s" /> 읍의 포고꾼이 알렸다 검은 가죽 지갑 하나를 잃어버렸다고. <break time="0.8s" /> 그날 아침. <break time="0.8s" /> 뵈즈빌로 가는 길에서. <break time="0.8s" /> 그 안에는 500프랑이 들어 있었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 사업 서류 몇 장도. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 찾은 사람은 받게 된다고 했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 20프랑의 사례금을. <break time="0.8s" /> 주인인 망빌 마을의 울브레크 영감은. <break time="0.8s" /> 찾은 사람에게 부탁했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그것을 읍장 사무실이나 자기에게 가져다 달라고. <break time="0.8s" /> 식사하던 사람들이 짐작하고 있을 때. <break time="0.8s" /> 누가 그것을 찾을지. <break time="0.8s" /> 경찰관 한 사람이 나타났다. <break time="0.8s" /> 식당 문간에. <break time="0.8s" /> 그는 브레오테의 오슈코른 영감을 찾았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 그에게 전했다 읍장님이 그와 이야기하고 싶어 한다고. <break time="0.8s" /> 당장.

Surprised and uneasy. <break time="0.8s" /> Hauchecorne swallowed his drink. <break time="0.8s" /> And followed the officer. <break time="0.8s" /> To the mayors office. <break time="0.8s" /> The mayor, a large, serious man. <break time="0.8s" /> Told him that someone had seen him. <break time="0.8s" /> Pick up the lost pocketbook. <break time="0.8s" /> When Hauchecorne asked. <break time="0.8s" /> Who had said such a thing. <break time="0.8s" /> The mayor answered. <break time="0.8s" /> Monsieur Malandain, the harness maker. <break time="0.8s" /> Red with anger. <break time="0.8s" /> The old man pulled the string. <break time="0.8s" /> From his pocket. <break time="0.8s" /> And showed it to the mayor. <break time="0.8s" /> He saw me pick up this string. <break time="0.8s" /> And that is the reason why I bent down. <break time="0.8s" /> He cried. <break time="0.8s" /> The mayor shook his head. <break time="0.8s" /> And said that an honest man like Malandain. <break time="0.8s" /> Would never mistake a string for a pocketbook. <break time="0.8s" /> Hauchecorne raised his hand. <break time="0.8s" /> And swore on his honor. <break time="0.8s" /> Speaking as if God himself were listening. <break time="0.8s" /> The mayor added that he had searched the mud for a long time. <break time="0.8s" /> Looking for coins that had fallen out. <break time="0.8s" /> Malandain was brought in and repeated his story. <break time="0.8s" /> And the two men argued angrily. <break time="0.8s" /> For a whole hour. <break time="0.8s" /> They searched Hauchecorne. <break time="0.8s" /> At his own request. <break time="0.8s" /> But found nothing. <break time="0.8s" /> So the puzzled mayor. <break time="0.8s" /> Let him go for now.

놀라고 불안한 마음으로. <break time="0.8s" /> 오슈코른은 술을 꿀꺽 삼켰다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 경찰관을 따라갔다. <break time="0.8s" /> 읍장 사무실로. <break time="0.8s" /> 읍장은 몸집이 크고 근엄한 사람이었는데. <break time="0.8s" /> 그에게 말했다 누군가 그를 보았다고. <break time="0.8s" /> 잃어버린 지갑을 줍는 것을. <break time="0.8s" /> 오슈코른이 묻자. <break time="0.8s" /> 누가 그런 말을 했느냐고. <break time="0.8s" /> 읍장이 대답했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 마구 장인 말랑댕 씨요. <break time="0.8s" /> 화가 나서 얼굴이 시뻘개진 채. <break time="0.8s" /> 노인은 끈을 꺼냈다. <break time="0.8s" /> 주머니에서. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 그것을 읍장에게 보여 주었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그 사람은 내가 이 끈을 줍는 걸 본 거요. <break time="0.8s" /> 내가 허리를 굽힌 건 바로 그 때문이란 말이오. <break time="0.8s" /> 그가 외쳤다. <break time="0.8s" /> 읍장은 고개를 저었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 말했다 말랑댕처럼 정직한 사람이. <break time="0.8s" /> 끈을 지갑으로 잘못 볼 리가 없다고. <break time="0.8s" /> 오슈코른은 손을 들었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 자기 명예를 걸고 맹세했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 마치 하느님이 직접 듣고 계신 것처럼 말하면서. <break time="0.8s" /> 읍장은 덧붙여 말했다 그가 오랫동안 진흙 바닥을 뒤졌다고. <break time="0.8s" /> 떨어져 나온 동전을 찾으면서. <break time="0.8s" /> 말랑댕이 불려 왔다 그리고 자기 이야기를 되풀이했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 두 사람은 화를 내며 말다툼했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 꼬박 한 시간 동안. <break time="0.8s" /> 사람들이 오슈코른의 몸을 뒤졌다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그 자신의 요청에 따라. <break time="0.8s" /> 하지만 아무것도 찾지 못했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그래서 난처해진 읍장은. <break time="0.8s" /> 일단 그를 보내 주었다.
